card: This pull request adds an AddrPolicy callback to AddrMan::GetAddr so callers can filter addresses during selection instead of removing them afterward. CConnman::GetAddressesUnsafe previously fetched a batch of addresses and then stripped banned and discouraged nodes, causing P2P GETADDR responses and the getnodeaddresses RPC to return fewer addresses than requested when many banned peers were selected. By filtering during selection, AddrMan continues searching until the requested quota is filled. The author demonstrates that banning a large set of addresses caused getnodeaddresses 1 to return empty results before this change.
evidence: PR description: Repro: ban or discourage a large set of addresses, then call getnodeaddresses 1, previously underfilled. After this change, the RPC returns up to the requested count as expected.
problem: Previously, CConnman::GetAddressesUnsafe() fetched a target number of addresses from AddrMan and then erased banned and discouraged addresses from the result. When many banned or discouraged addresses were selected, callers like getnodeaddresses and P2P GETADDR handlers received fewer addresses than requested or none at all, even if AddrMan held plenty of valid alternatives.
scope_notes: The callback is executed inside AddrManImpl::GetAddr_ while holding AddrMan::cs, introducing a lock acquisition order of AddrMan::cs followed by BanMan::m_banned_mutex.
summary: Introduces an AddrPolicy predicate callback to AddrMan::GetAddr() to filter out addresses during selection rather than post-processing. CConnman::GetAddressesUnsafe() uses this callback to skip banned and discouraged peers while populating the requested address quota. AddrMan also logs the breakdown of addresses filtered by network, quality, and policy.
